stories.label: Finnish border guards head towards drone-hit cargo ship
stories.summary: A cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad was hit by two drones in the Gulf of Finland, three nautical miles from Russia's border, and is now burning in Finnish waters with its crew being evacuated. Lead with where it happened: the war at sea has reached the Baltic route that keeps Russia's exclave supplied, beside a NATO member's coast. Attribute Russian officials' account and the Kaliningrad governor's 'no threat to supplies' line to TASS; Finland's border guard is the independent voice. Nobody has claimed it — say so. Dateline Gulf of Finland / Helsinki.

stories.label: Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
stories.summary: Follow-up to our 11-20 story on the suspected missile in Lublin province. The new development: Warsaw now says it may have been hit by two missiles, security cameras caught the impact, and the government calls it an intentional Russian provocation, not stray debris. Lead with that shift from 'investigating' to an accusation. Then explain the mechanism: what Article 4 consultations and Article 5 each require, and why the bar for collective defence stays high. Dateline Warsaw.

stories.label: Ballistic missile attack on Zelenskyy's hometown kills two people
stories.summary: A Russian ballistic missile on Kryvyi Rih killed a seven-year-old boy and a young paramedic. Lead with the two dead by name if the sources give them, and with the paramedic: a responder killed in a city that has been hit again and again. The mechanism: ballistic missiles give minutes or none of warning, so air defence and shelters fail first in cities near the front. Note Zelensky calling Putin a 'killer' while Washington courts Moscow over a January deal deadline. Dateline Kryvyi Rih.

stories.label: COP31: Nigerian, global groups accuse presidencies of risking 'disappointing' climate deal
stories.summary: As COP31 in Antalya runs into its final hours, a coalition of 100 civil society groups led from Nigeria says the joint Türkiye–Australia presidency failed to steer the talks, letting climate finance, adaptation and the fossil-fuel transition weaken. Lead with who is speaking: Global South groups whose countries carry the cost of warming they did not cause. The mechanism: a split presidency with no single broker. This follows our stories on the draft dropping fossil-fuel language and on net-negative emissions. Dateline Antalya.

stories.label: Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least four in Nigeria
stories.summary: A boat believed to carry hundreds of mourners to a funeral capsized in Bayelsa State after a mechanical failure; at least four are dead, two of them children, and the search goes on. Lead with the gap between hundreds aboard and four counted. The mechanism: in the creeks of the Niger Delta boats are the only road, and overloading and missing life jackets go unenforced, so capsizes recur every year. Dateline Bayelsa State.

stories.label: Minister clashes with BBC host on UK-EU tuition fees talks - 'you're the expert'
stories.summary: Report the substance, not the radio row: Friday's UK-EU summit agreed deals that ministers insist are not at risk, while a dispute over what EU students pay at British universities hangs over them. Lead with what was agreed at the summit and what Brussels wants on tuition fees in return. The mechanism: the EU ties market access to youth mobility and fee parity, so a university-funding question becomes a trade lever. Who pays: UK universities that rely on higher international fees. Dateline London.

stories.label: ETH news: Ether's plunge puts a Nasdaq-listed treasury in a $54 million loan squeeze
stories.summary: BTCS, a Nasdaq-listed company whose main asset is ether, told the SEC it cannot rule out liquidation of a $54 million Aave loan backed by that ether, even after paying down about $10 million in ten days. Lead with the filing. The mechanism: 'crypto treasury' firms borrowed against the coin they hold, so a falling price shrinks the collateral and can force a sale that pushes the price lower. Context: bitcoin at a two-year low after the Fed's hikes. Dateline New York.

stories.label: Signal Cracks Down on AI Agents, Says They Threaten Users' Privacy
stories.summary: Signal is blocking OS-level AI agents such as Google's Gemini and Apple's Siri from screen-capturing its chats. Lead with the threat model: end-to-end encryption protects a message in transit, but an assistant that reads the screen takes it after decryption, at the operating-system layer the app does not control. Who is exposed: the journalists, officials and dissidents who rely on Signal. Explain what Signal can block and what it cannot.

stories.label: Denmark's GomSpace Secures €8M Contract for Blue Origin Moon Mission
stories.summary: Danish satellite maker GomSpace won an €8 million phase-two contract to build two spacecraft for a lunar resource-prospecting mission. Its announcement names only a 'leading North American' customer; European Spaceflight identifies it as Blue Origin. Lead with the hidden customer and what the craft are meant to prospect for. The structural point: European small-satellite firms are becoming suppliers to a US-led race to claim resources on the Moon. Dateline Aalborg.

stories.label: An ancient failed rift is reawakening inside one of Africa's oldest landmasses
stories.summary: The magnitude 6.5 earthquake of April 2017 in eastern Botswana came from the middle of the Kalahari Craton, crust up to 3.7 billion years old that geologists thought too cold and thick to tear. New work finds an ancient failed rift there reactivating. Lead with that 2017 quake and why it should not have happened. The mechanism: what is weakening the old rift. Why it matters: seismic hazard in a region whose buildings were never designed for it. Dateline Gaborone.

stories.label: Scientists Discover New and Horrible Eagle-Based Way Our Ancestors Died
stories.summary: Researchers documented eagles in Chad hunting large adult baboons, prey far heavier than thought possible. That suggests birds of prey threatened early humans and other hominins later in our evolution than believed. Lead with the observed kill and the animal's size. The mechanism: what talon marks on fossil skulls, like the Taung child's, now mean when read against live behaviour. Dateline Chad.

stories.label: What makes rock deep beneath continents break away and sink?
stories.summary: Dense rock at the base of the crust can detach and sink hundreds of kilometres into the mantle — 'lithospheric dripping' — the opposite of how we picture mountain building; seismic images suggest it happened under the central Andes and the Sierra Nevada. Lead with the new study's finding on what triggers the drip and what it does at the surface (uplift, volcanism).

stories.label: Countries open path towards 'killer robots' pact
stories.summary: UN talks in Geneva under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons ended without a legally binding ban on lethal autonomous weapons; states only agreed to keep negotiating for two more years. Lead with the gap: autonomous drones are already in use in Ukraine, Gaza and Sudan while the treaty runs on consensus, so the states building these weapons (US, Russia) can block any ban. Name who blocked and who pushed for a ban; Pakistan's Dawn and TRT carry the Global South position.

stories.label: Three El Salvador soldiers die in explosives accident in Haiti
stories.summary: Three Salvadoran soldiers died handling explosives in Haiti, part of a contingent Bukele sent last month to rescue four missing airmen that has since widened into an operation against Haiti's gangs — and Haiti has just struck a deal for El Salvador to build it new prisons. Lead with the mission creep: a rescue deployment turning into Bukele exporting his mass-incarceration model to Haiti, with Haitians who live under the gangs as the people it lands on.

stories.label: FBI Most Wanted drug lord 'El Chapo Isidro' reportedly arrested in Mexico as violence erupts- Moneycontrol.com
stories.summary: Mexican soldiers captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, 'Chapo Isidro', one of the FBI's ten most wanted, in Sinaloa; the gunfight that followed sent civilians, including fans at a stadium, running. Lead with who bears the cost: the capture of a kingpin under US pressure sets off violence that Sinaloa residents absorb, as previous captures have fractured cartels into new wars. Datelined Sinaloa, not Washington.

stories.label: Oil shipped through Hormuz falls as Iranian strikes increase
stories.summary: Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has started falling again — 263 vessels in the week to November — as near-daily Iranian strikes on ships make the recovery in Gulf crude exports 'increasingly fragile'. New since our tanker-fire and mine-claims stories: the IRGC says it shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the strait and Washington sanctioned four Iranians it calls 'oil trustees' (Al Jazeera). Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude; lead with the transit count and who pays — Gulf exporters and Asian importers.

stories.label: 中国车企在印度，工厂、股权与供应链
stories.summary: Chinese carmakers in India, from the mainland tech press: factories, equity stakes and supply chains — Mahindra's electric cars run on BYD battery cells. Lead with that detail: despite New Delhi's post-Galwan curbs on Chinese investment, India's EV push depends on Chinese cells and components, routed through joint ventures and minority stakes. Give the Chinese industry's own view of the market, not only India's security framing.

stories.label: Bitcoin developers fix 'medium' bug that could have delayed transactions
stories.summary: Bitcoin Core shipped a fix for a bug that could temporarily stall a node — found not by a human auditor but by Loupe, an open-source AI-agent code scanner from Block's Spiral. Lead with the shift it marks: AI agents now finding flaws in the software that secures a trillion-dollar network, and maintainers patching before anyone exploits them. Distinct from our earlier wallet-nonce story.

stories.label: Alcaldía de Marcovia sigue los pasos del Distrito Central y compra servicios por casi dos millones de lempiras a la misma empresa de IA
stories.summary: A second Honduran municipality, Marcovia, paid 1.92 million lempiras (about $71,000) to Gobai Ventures, the firm that runs Tegucigalpa's AI unit — and when Contracorriente tested Marcovia's new virtual assistant, it said it only took reports from the capital. Lead with that test: public money buying a rebadged chatbot that does not serve the town that paid for it, and one AI vendor spreading through local governments.

stories.label: Mobilfunk aus dem All: Kampf um die digitale Zukunft
stories.summary: Direct-to-phone mobile service from orbit is becoming a fight over who controls communications: Starlink alone holds over 10,000 satellites in low orbit. Lead with the sovereignty stake — whoever runs satellite-to-cell service sets the terms on which societies communicate, including where ground networks are cut by war or shutdowns — and what Europe and others are doing about dependence on one US company.

stories.label: [c2]Daisy-chain molecular turing machines with switchable fluorescence outputs
stories.summary: Chemists built synthetic small molecules linked in a daisy chain that behave like a Turing machine: reversible reactions shift the chain between states, and the result is read out as switchable fluorescence. Lead with the idea of computation done by single molecules rather than circuits, and say plainly how far it is from anything practical.

stories.label: Trump vows to punish U.S. firms building data centres abroad
stories.summary: Trump threatened a 'tremendous tax' on US companies that build AI data centres outside the US, framed as keeping the AI lead from China. Lead with who it lands on: the Gulf, Malaysia, India and Southeast Asian hosts courting US hyperscaler capex — and the power-grid constraint at home that pushed builds abroad. Name what is a threat versus an actual instrument; no decision is attached yet.

stories.label: Bayer's $7.25bn settlement over cancer cases approved by US judge
stories.summary: A US judge approved Bayer's $7.25bn class settlement of tens of thousands of claims that Roundup (glyphosate) caused non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Lead with the accountability mechanism: a class deal that also binds future claimants, capping a liability Bayer bought with Monsanto in 2018 — and that glyphosate stays on sale. Who is paid, how much per claimant, and who gave up the right to a jury.

stories.label: Punjab fixes wheat release price
stories.summary: Punjab set the wheat release price at Rs4,500 per 40kg for flour mills and capped a 10kg flour bag at Rs1,275, with mandatory digital monitoring and daily reporting — the government's answer to the 10% weekly jump in flour that led last week's inflation reading. Lead with what a family pays for atta and whether a release price from state stocks can hold a retail cap; tie to wheat prices and Sindh's cut earlier this month.

stories.label: US should explicitly state its desire to enter into peace agreement with Iran -- Araghchi
stories.summary: Araghchi says Tehran wants a deal that 'ensures there is no further war' and an explicit US statement that it seeks peace before talks — a shift in tone from the seven preconditions Rezaei set on 11-10 and Ghalibaf's closure-until-conditions line. Lead with what Iran is now asking for and what it no longer demands; context: mined Hormuz, third US carrier, Pakistani mediation. TASS is the second source — attribute it.

stories.label: Iran exaggerates Hormuz sea mine threat but uses fear to tighten grip | The National
stories.summary: Naval experts say the IRGC's daily claims of ships hitting mines do not stand up to scrutiny — yet the fear alone is keeping crews and insurers out. This reframes two weeks of 'tanker hits mine' reports: the weapon may be the announcement. Lead with which claimed hits are unverified, and what it costs anyway — ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and war-risk premiums.

stories.label: 'We ​are tired from all this suffering': displaced families in Gaza brace for another winter of misery
stories.summary: Floods have already collapsed sandbanks beside tent camps as Gaza's displaced face another winter under a ceasefire the Board of Peace says has collapsed. Lead with a named family (Abdul Karim al-Sahhar) and the numbers: how many still in tents, what shelter material Israel lets in and what it blocks. Continuation of the siege is the development.

stories.label: Ukrainian children under Russian occupation are abducted, tortured and forced to fight for Russia
stories.summary: About 1.6 million children live in Russian-occupied Ukraine; Ukraine's human rights commissioner Lubinets says boys are abducted, tortured and conscripted to fight against their own country. Lead with the documented cases and the mechanism of Russification (passports, schools, military-patriotic camps, conscription at 18) — and attribute the commissioner's figures as Ukrainian government claims. Timely as Kushner's Ukraine security-guarantee talks advance.

stories.label: 深夜，美股AI血崩，英伟达市值已跌去2.7万亿美元
stories.summary: Friday's US close is the new development after Asia's slide: the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 10.7% (43% off its June peak), Nvidia 14% (seventh straight loss, $2.74tn erased since 6 October), Micron 14%, TSMC 9%, ASML 7%, Nasdaq-100 5.6% for its worst week in six years, VIX to 40. The trigger to lead with: Reuters reports the SEC is investigating Nvidia's accounting, on top of Huang's exit and Fed hike fears; the US 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.94% as money fled to safety. Explains the Micron, TSMC and ASML moves.

stories.label: 27B！穆拉蒂开源“循环脑”模型：笔记本跑Agent起飞！
stories.summary: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab released open weights for Inkling 2 Mini, a 27B mixture-of-experts 'looped' transformer whose middle 12 layers run three times per token — about 20GB, it runs on a laptop. Lead with the safety question TML itself raised: looping lets a model reason without writing it into its chain of thought, so it may be harder to monitor; they released a 1–5 loop research model so outsiders can test that. Benchmarks vs Qwen3.8-27B as context, not the lead.

stories.label: Hackers reportedly breach FBI crime database -- the 2nd time the bureau was targeted in months
stories.summary: Hackers breached the FBI's National Crime Information Center, the database every US police force queries for warrants, stolen property and watchlists — the bureau's second breach in months, per CNN. Lead with what NCIC holds and who is exposed (informants, protected persons, people on terrorism watchlists); attribute everything as reported, the FBI has confirmed only an investigation.

stories.label: Assassination Plot: Danes Expel Russian Diplomat
stories.summary: Denmark is expelling Russia's defence attaché in Copenhagen after accusing Moscow of being behind an attempt to assassinate a Ukrainian rapper on Danish soil, and says it is weighing suspending Schengen visas for Russians. Lead with the named target and the named diplomat; the mechanism is Russian intelligence running lethal operations on NATO territory, the same week Poland reported three airspace violations and Estonia shut its border crossings.

stories.label: Mamdani unveils plan to close New York's Rikers Island by 2032
stories.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani set a 2032 date to close Rikers Island, replacing it with about 4,100 cells in borough jails, which means shrinking the jail population. Lead with the gap between the cells planned and the people held today, and with the people who have died in Rikers custody. The New York Post's attack is opinion: use it only as the counterpoint, not as a source of fact.

stories.label: Indian man jailed over US murder plot against Sikh separatist
stories.summary: A US court sentenced Nikhil Gupta to more than 19 years for plotting to hire a hitman to kill Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun on US soil, allegedly on behalf of Indian intelligence; New Delhi denies involvement. Lead with the sentence; the mechanism is transnational repression, where a state uses criminal proxies against diaspora critics. It is the same day Denmark expelled a Russian attaché over an assassination plot.

stories.label: CTD says 3 terrorists, including mastermind of Kohat police lines attack, killed in IBO
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Counter Terrorism Department says it killed three members of the banned Ittehadul Mujahideen Pakistan, including the planner of September's Kohat Police Lines attack. This is the CTD's claim and the article must attribute it. Explain who the IMP is and why police in the province are its targets.

stories.label: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 level
stories.summary: The new development since this morning's ETF-outflow story: bitcoin fell as much as 6.1% to $57,716, its lowest since September 2024, as investors sold crypto, stocks and gold together to hold cash ahead of expected Fed rate hikes. Lead with the two-year low and the round trip from the post-election rally. Chart bitcoin. CoinDesk merged in for the flight-to-cash mechanism.

stories.label: Japan sovereign AI project faces $5bn cost surge on chip prices, weak yen
stories.summary: The cost of Noetra, Japan's sovereign AI consortium of 44 companies including SoftBank, may rise by up to 800 billion yen ($5 billion), Nikkei reports, because GPUs are priced in dollars and the yen is weak. Lead with the figure. The mechanism is a country that wants AI independence still buying it in a currency it doesn't control. Chart the yen.

stories.label: The smile-inducing 'Reis' exchange between Minister Bayraktar and Pakistani officials
stories.summary: Skip the anecdote in the headline. The news is that Turkey's seismic research vessel Oruç Reis has arrived in Karachi, welcomed by Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar, to survey Pakistan's offshore waters for oil and gas after earlier surveys off Somalia. Lead with what it will survey and the terms of the Turkey–Pakistan deal. The mechanism is an energy importer betting on offshore discoveries to cut a fuel bill driven by the Gulf war, with Turkey exporting its exploration capacity across the Muslim world.

stories.label: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers
stories.summary: Meta's own sustainability report says it is 're-evaluating' its 2030 net-zero pledge after a record jump in greenhouse emissions driven by AI data centres. Lead with the size of the rise in emissions. The mechanism: the AI buildout is turning corporate climate pledges into costs firms now decline to pay, while COP31 in Antalya argues the world must go net negative.

stories.label: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental? | New Scientist
stories.summary: A claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis, one of the Clay Institute's $1 million Millennium Prize problems, was reached by mathematicians working with Anthropic's Claude. Say plainly that the proof is unverified until mathematicians check it. Explain what the hypothesis says about how the primes are spaced, and what the AI contributed versus the humans. Public attention is high: Dario Amodei is among yesterday's most-read Wikipedia pages.

stories.label: Net zero emissions won't reverse climate change -- some nations look to 'net negative'
stories.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, more countries now accept that net zero only stops warming from rising, and that bringing temperatures down needs net-negative emissions: removing more CO2 than is emitted. Lead with the physics of why net zero leaves the warming already locked in. Then the hard part: who pays for removal at scale, and which countries are pushing it. This follows our story on the COP31 draft dropping the fossil-fuel transition language.

stories.label: Caribbean corals are in crisis. Fossil reefs can help point to where corals may persist
stories.summary: In two new papers, UT Austin researchers read the fossil reefs that sit metres from living corals in northeastern Jamaica to find which species dominated before the last 70 years of decline. Lead with the idea that the old reefs work as a map of where corals may survive warming. Name the species and what it means for restoring reefs that Caribbean fishing communities depend on.

stories.label: Quantum effect could reverse gravity and violate Einstein's theory of relativity | New Scientist
stories.summary: Two mathematical studies, one involving Oxford's Vlatko Vedral, show that a mass in quantum superposition could in principle make gravity repel instead of attract. Say clearly that this is theory with no experiment yet. Lead with what would have to be true for gravity to push, and explain why it matters: it is a possible tabletop test of whether gravity is quantum at all.

stories.label: A leaky AI supply chain is exposing secret user data at an alarming rate
stories.summary: Researchers planted 2 million traceable secrets in prompts sent through AI routers, resellers and inference providers, and found many of the secrets later surfaced where they shouldn't. Lead with the leak rate. The mechanism: an API call to 'a model' passes through intermediaries that users never see and cannot audit. The reader is a developer who pastes keys and code into these services.

stories.label: Mysterious MQ-25 Stingray-Like Chinese Drone Emerges At Little-Known Flight Test Center
stories.summary: Satellite imagery shows an unidentified Chinese drone, shaped like the US Navy's MQ-25 Stingray carrier-based refueller, at an obscure Chinese flight-test facility. Lead with what the imagery shows. Explain why a carrier tanker drone matters: it extends how far carrier jets can fly from the ship, which is the reach China needs at sea. Keep to what the imagery shows; this is OSINT, not an official reveal.

stories.label: Google's latest search page redesign drops the search button, adds AI sidebar
stories.summary: Google's desktop homepage drops the 'Google Search' button and adds a persistent AI sidebar. Lead with the removal of the button. The structural point is that the world's dominant entry point to the web is steering queries into AI answers. That cuts traffic to the publishers whose pages it summarises, and it deepens the regulators' complaint about Google's control of search.

stories.label: Trump administration wants Ukraine and Russia to reach peace deal by January 2027
stories.summary: After Berlin talks with Zelensky and the Coalition of the Willing, envoy Jared Kushner says Moscow appears ready to accept NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine, and Washington wants a deal by January 2027. Lead with the guarantee claim and the deadline; explain what a guarantee short of NATO membership means, who would enforce it, and what Ukraine is being asked to give up. Ukrainska Pravda carries Kyiv's reading. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: Spanish PM Sanchez admits to 'mistakes' 10 days before elections
stories.summary: In the only televised debate before Spain's election, Pedro Sánchez conceded 'mistakes' as Alberto Núñez Feijóo hit him on corruption cases and housing. Lead with the admission and the two issues that decide the vote; explain what is at stake: whether the PP needs Vox to govern, and what that means for one of Europe's few governments that recognised Palestine. Anadolu and the Express Tribune give the non-European read. Dateline Madrid.

stories.label: Estonia to Close Russian Border as Moscow Threatens Response
stories.summary: Estonia will shut every land crossing with Russia on 1 December for at least six months, and Moscow's foreign ministry promises a response. Lead with the closure date and who it strands: Narva's Russian-speaking residents and families split across the river. Explain why Tallinn is doing it now, the same day Poland reports three Russian objects in its airspace, and treat Moscow's warning as TASS reports it. Dateline Tallinn.

stories.label: Tanker catches fire after projectile strike near Strait of Hormuz - UKMTO
stories.summary: New since our 19 November LNG story: a tanker caught fire after a projectile hit it 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, by UKMTO's account, while Iran moves crude ship-to-ship to test the US blockade (Al-Monitor). Lead with the strike. The surprise is that Brent crude is still heading for a third weekly loss, below $91, because returning Gulf supply outweighs the war risk. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude as the series. Dateline Khasab.

stories.label: Sudan’s Power Grid on Brink of Collapse Following Wave of Strikes Targeting Electricity Stations
stories.summary: A wave of drone strikes on Sudan's power stations has left the national grid near collapse: hospitals are running without power, farms cannot pump water, and repair is not in sight. Lead with what has gone dark and who pays: civilians in army-held cities. Name who is hitting the stations and why infrastructure has become the target in the SAF–RSF war. This is the Sudan coverage the daily audit says is missing. Dateline Port Sudan unless the report places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Houthis say they attacked power plant, port in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: The Houthis' spokesman Yahya Saree claims strikes on a Saudi power plant and port, as retaliation for coalition strikes on power plants in Saada and Mokha and the shelling of a Hodeidah port berth. Lead with the tit-for-tat on power infrastructure, which the cost of the war has now reached on both sides of the border. The only source is Russian state agency TASS relaying a Houthi claim: attribute every claim and state nothing as fact. Dateline Sanaa.

stories.label: Protests held across Europe over wages, services, high living costs
stories.summary: Workers and students rallied in 25 European countries, on the model of France's protests, against high living costs, stagnant wages and military spending crowding out public services. Italy's CGIL is out in Rome. Lead with how far the protests have spread and the trade-off they name: governments raising defence budgets while wages and services fall behind. Dateline Rome.

stories.label: Live news: Bitcoin hovers just above $61,000 as Anthropic slides 13% after Nasdaq debut
stories.summary: The US AI selloff has spread to Asia: South Korea's Kospi fell more than 5%, the market that holds Samsung and SK Hynix, while Anthropic is down 13% from its Nasdaq debut. Lead with the Kospi drop and the memory-chip names; this is the move behind Samsung's 11% and TSMC's 15% weekly falls. Explain the mechanism, doubt about AI capex flowing back to the chipmakers, and leave bitcoin as a secondary line since our ETF-outflow story already reported it. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: Valve says it might have to raise the price of supply-limited Steam Machines
stories.summary: Valve says it may raise the Steam Machine's price again because it still cannot buy RAM and storage at a reasonable cost. Lead with the mechanism: the AI data-centre build-out has absorbed the memory supply, and the cost now lands on consumer hardware. Tie it to the memory makers (Micron, Samsung) whose shares fell this week, and show how a shortage priced for hyperscalers reaches an ordinary buyer.

stories.label: Amazon says Chinese hackers used Cairn AI tool to discover apparent zero-day during attack on university
stories.summary: Amazon researchers say a China-linked group used Cairn, an open-source AI penetration-testing tool, to keep attacking two universities, and in one case it may have found a zero-day on its own. Lead with the possible AI-found zero-day. That is the threshold security people have been waiting for: offensive AI that no longer needs a skilled operator. Attribute the attribution to Amazon.

stories.label: Tencent releases Hy4 model weights with million-token context
stories.summary: Tencent has released the weights of its flagship Hy4 model under Apache 2.0, with a million-token context and text, image and video understanding, so anyone can download it, deploy it and build on it commercially. Lead with the licence. China's largest labs keep giving away frontier-class weights while US labs close theirs, and this is how Chinese models win developers worldwide. Dateline Shenzhen.

stories.label: Kids Act: EU-Datenschutzbehörde warnt vor Alterskontrollen
stories.summary: The European Data Protection Supervisor calls the Commission's planned online age checks in the Kids Act unnecessary and immature, and lists ten objections. Lead with the EU's own privacy watchdog opposing the Commission. The mechanism: verifying age means identifying every user, adults included, to protect children. Pick the two or three objections with the most consequence. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: German attack drones pass live-fire tests, with first deliveries planned this year
stories.summary: Germany's procurement office says two one-way attack drone variants, including Helsing's HX-2, passed live-fire trials, and deliveries and troop training will start before year end. Lead with Germany fielding loitering munitions of the kind Ukraine's war made standard. Explain who builds them, what software-defined targeting means, and how fast Berlin moved from hesitancy to buying them. Dateline Koblenz.

stories.label: Spiders, beetles and one garage alligator: Largest study to date reveals wildlife sharing our indoor spaces
stories.summary: The largest survey yet of life inside homes catalogues more than 2,000 species in over 20,000 records from the US and Canada. Lead with the scale: the house is an ecosystem. Explain what the database lets scientists study, such as pest spread, allergens and the species that now live only indoors, and name the journal.

stories.label: Malaysia plans to resettle 10,000 Rohingya in Turkiye
stories.summary: Malaysia, which hosts some of the largest Rohingya population outside Bangladesh without recognising them as refugees, will move 10,000 to Turkey through a skills-training scheme: one of the biggest Rohingya resettlements since the 2017 Rakhine crackdown. Lead with the number and the mechanism (labour-skills channel rather than refugee status), and why two Muslim-majority states are doing what Western resettlement programmes have not. Follow-up context: it comes days after the ICJ found Myanmar forces killed some 10,000 Rohingya; dateline Kuala Lumpur.

stories.label: El Salvador's Bukele to run for third presidential term
stories.summary: Bukele registered with the Supreme Electoral Court for a third term, which the constitution once barred outright; lead with the registration itself and the 'six more years' crowd. The mechanism: a loyalist legislature and a court he reshaped removed the term limits, and the state of exception that jailed tens of thousands keeps his approval high. Who bears the cost: detainees held without trial and an opposition with no institutional check left. Dateline San Salvador.

stories.label: French Ex-PM Villepin Announces Presidential Run
stories.summary: Dominique de Villepin, the prime minister remembered for France's 2003 UN stand against the Iraq invasion and a vocal critic of the war on Gaza, enters the 2027 race decrying a 'decaying' France. Lead with what his candidacy puts on the ballot: a Gaullist foreign-policy line in a field where the far right leads and the centre has fragmented. Asharq Al-Awsat carries the regional view. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Afghanistan not invited to ECO moot as Islamabad does not recognise Kabul regime: FO
stories.summary: Pakistan, hosting the Economic Cooperation Organisation's foreign ministers in Islamabad, left Afghanistan off the invitation list because it does not recognise the Taliban government, shutting a founding regional member out of a trade and connectivity bloc. Lead with the exclusion and the stated reason; the mechanism is that Pakistan-Taliban relations have broken down over cross-border militant attacks and closed crossings, and Afghan traders and transit routes bear the cost. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $582M in a Day as BTC Drops Below $62K
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $62,000, down 10% in a week, as BlackRock's bitcoin fund posted a record outflow and spot ETFs shed $582 million in a day. The cause is the point: bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike and a US tech sell-off that spread to Asia, the same move behind the week's fall in TSMC, Samsung and Micron. Lead with the record outflow, then the mechanism: the ETFs that tied bitcoin to Wall Street now carry the Fed's rate path straight into it. Chart: bitcoin.

stories.label: Short-term inflation reaches 10.41pc on costly flour
stories.summary: Pakistan's weekly price index rose 10.41% year on year, driven by wheat flour. Lead with flour: the staple of the poorest households, whose cost lands hardest on them. Mechanism: a poor regional wheat crop (India's sowing fell the most in 26 years) and fuel costs feeding through. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Bank of Russia's gold reserves decrease by 0.3 million troy ounces
stories.summary: The Bank of Russia's gold holdings fell to 72.5 million troy ounces in October, the lowest since October 2019, according to central bank data reported by Russian state news agency TASS (attribute it so). Mechanism: with Western sanctions freezing its foreign-currency reserves, gold is the reserve Moscow can actually spend, and the National Wealth Fund has been selling it to cover a war-swollen budget deficit. Chart: gold. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: Astronomers reveal the oceanic origin of Europa's sodium cloud
stories.summary: Two decades of Keck Observatory measurements show the sodium cloud around Jupiter's moon Europa has stayed strikingly stable despite Jupiter's violent environment, which points to a steady source: salt from the ocean under the ice. Lead with the 20-year stability and why it implicates the ocean rather than Io's volcanoes; what's next is NASA's Europa Clipper, arriving 2030, which can test it. Dateline Maunakea, Hawaii.

stories.label: US science academy urges journals to fix errors more quickly
stories.summary: A National Academies report finds journals take too long to retract or correct flawed papers and apply inconsistent standards, and that nobody even collects data on how long it takes. Lead with that missing number. Mechanism: publishers have little incentive to retract, so flawed results keep being cited and built on, in medicine as elsewhere. Name the recommendations and who must act on them. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: BTC news: Bitcoin wallet mistakes exposed $106 million to thieves, researchers find
stories.summary: Researchers found wallet software reusing or mis-generating the signature nonce, an old cryptographic mistake that lets anyone compute the private key from the blockchain; vulnerable addresses held up to about $106 million. When the researchers exposed keys of their own as bait, bots drained them within seconds. Lead with the seconds-long sweep; the mechanism is one bad random number in a signature; be precise that how much was actually stolen is not established.

stories.label: Trump admin still won't let Wi-Fi giant TP-Link sell its latest routers in US
stories.summary: TP-Link, likely the top supplier of routers to US homes and small businesses, still cannot sell its newest Wi-Fi models in the US under the administration's sweeping ban on foreign-made communications equipment. Lead with the market share frozen out; the mechanism is equipment authorisation at the FCC used as a gate, and the cost falls on buyers left with older, less secure hardware. Name what the company has done to comply and what the government asks in return.

stories.label: AI时代，华为要再造一个“荣耀”！首款鸿蒙AI手机来了
stories.summary: Huawei launched OSTA, its first new phone sub-brand since it was forced to sell Honor in 2020, with the OSTA O1 Pro on its own Kirin 9030S chip and HarmonyOS 7: an agent-style assistant that books restaurants, sends WeChat messages and hails Didi from one spoken command, at 5,499 yuan. Lead with the comeback: six years after US sanctions cost it Honor, Huawei has rebuilt chips and an operating system at home and is splitting into two brands again. Inside view from mainland tech press. Dateline Shenzhen.
